# stelow-host-multica

> Provision [stelow](https://github.com/calionauta/stelow) onto a
> [Multica](https://multica.ai) workspace with the `multica` CLI: three
> workflows (build, explore, research), the agents that run them, and exactly
> the skills each agent needs. A provisioner, not a plugin — no runtime, no
> daemon, no UI.

## Start here

- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) — the install runbook (prerequisites, command order,
  what success and failure look like), the commands, and the rules that keep
  this repository honest.
- [README.md](README.md) — what it does, why three workflows, and what has been
  verified live.
- [docs/boards.md](docs/boards.md) — lanes: what a lane is, which lane a card is
  on, how to add a skill or a fourth lane.
- [docs/host-contract.md](docs/host-contract.md) — the upstream contract this
  repository implements.
- [docs/operations.md](docs/operations.md) — running it on a live workspace and
  what a failed run looks like.

## The shortest correct path

```bash
export MULTICA_WORKSPACE_ID=<id> MULTICA_RUNTIME_ID=<id>
python3 bin/stelow-host sync
python3 bin/stelow-host board
python3 bin/stelow-host plan --all-workflows
python3 bin/stelow-host install --check
python3 bin/stelow-host install
python3 bin/stelow-host verify --all-workflows
```

## What is where

- `config/install.json` — the three workflows and the projects they bind to.
- `config/columns.json` — the chain: stage groups → columns → agents + support skills.
- `boards/explore.json`, `boards/research.json` — the lanes and their skill menus.
- `agents/*.md` — agent identity plus the Multica/state adapter.
- `stages/columns.md` — what each chain column asks of its handler.
- `bin/stelow-host` — the provisioner (`sync`, `plan`, `apply`, `install`, `ask`,
  `board`, `verify`, `status`, `card`, `doctor`).
- `tests/run.py` — the suite; no network.

## Non-negotiables

- The stage list, intent routes and stage→skill ownership come from the pinned
  stelow release (`stages.yaml`, `stage-catalog.json`), never from this repo.
- Every step names the skills it runs; a step that does not makes the agent
  improvise.
- `plan` before `apply`. No dependencies: python3 stdlib plus the `multica`
  binary.
- English only.
